question: After the current-base test repair, should OpenClaw adopt this Gateway-owned durable approval lifecycle and generic approval protocol/data model as the foundation for the stacked cross-surface rollout?
rationale: The implementation architecture appears sound, but the protected maintainer label and new persistent security-sensitive product contract require explicit owner acceptance.

options.title: Adopt after repair
options.body: Fix the stale assertion, clear attributable exact-head failures, and approve this foundation before reviewing stacked consumers separately.

options.title: Narrow the contract
options.body: Reduce the initial persistence or protocol surface before dependent PRs proceed.

options.title: Pause the rollout
options.body: Hold this PR and its stacked branches if durable cross-surface approvals are not the desired direction.

recommendation.title: Adopt after repair
recommendation.body: Fix the stale assertion, clear attributable exact-head failures, and approve this foundation before reviewing stacked consumers separately.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior merged approval and revocation work gives this owner the strongest available product and compatibility context.
